posts.title: The squeak of a naruko head
posts.excerpt: A naruko kokeshi's head turns with a small squeak. The sound comes from a peg cut a hair too tight.
posts.content:
A naruko kokeshi's head turns with a small squeak.

A hair too tight

The peg under the head is turned a fraction wider than the hole in the body, then pressed in with a twist. Too tight and the body splits; too loose and the doll is silent.

Every naruko doll is tried by ear before it is boxed.

posts.title: Why the wood waits two winters
posts.excerpt: Mizuki logs sit under the eaves for two winters before they reach the lathe, so the dolls never crack on a warm shelf.
posts.content:
Mizuki logs sit under the eaves for two winters before they reach the lathe.

Knock and listen

Green wood shrinks as it dries and splits around the head peg. A seasoned log rings when you knock it; that is the only test we use.

posts.title: A Saturday at the long table
posts.excerpt: Six guests, six blanks and one pot of red: notes from a painting class.
posts.content:
Six guests, six blanks and one pot of red.

Faces first

Everyone practises the face on washi ten times before painting it once on the wood. The best faces are the ones painted fastest.

posts.title: Striped togatta for autumn
posts.excerpt: The autumn togatta pairs have rings of moss green and red, painted while the doll spins on the lathe.
posts.content:
The autumn togatta pairs have rings of moss green and red.

Painting on the spin

The rings are painted with the brush held still and the doll turning, so each line closes on itself exactly.
